items.body: Register Login Wild Place Daemon Hunt On Waivers By Brennan McClain | at October 23, 2026 2:53 pm As the Minnesota Wild continue to reintroduce injured players to the lineup, other players will suffer the consequences. Today, that player is defenseman Daemon Hunt , whom the Wild announced they have placed on waivers. Presumably, Minnesota will assign Hunt to the AHL’s Iowa Wild if he clears. Given that he is strictly a depth defenseman, even at his age, the Wild shouldn’t have any issues passing him through the wire. In the NHL, Hunt has only played for Minnesota. The Wild selected him with the 65th overall pick in the 2020 NHL Draft. Since becoming a full-time professional player for the 2022-23 season, most of Hunt’s professional career has been spent in the Wild organization. Early into the 2024-25 season, Minnesota traded Hunt to the Columbus Blue Jackets as part of the package for David Jiříček . During his tenure with the Blue Jackets organization, he played only for the AHL’s Cleveland Monsters, scoring two goals and 14 points in 48 games with a -8 rating. He re-signed with Columbus the following offseason, but the Wild claimed him off waivers before the regular season. In a similar role, Hunt spent the entire 2025-26 season with Minnesota. He finished the campaign with six assists in 32 games with a -3 rating, averaging 12:26 of ice time per game. This year, Hunt has been held scoreless in 11 contests, while averaging 14:08 of ice time per night. If he is assigned to AHL Iowa after clearing waivers, it’ll be his first AHL appearance since the 2024-25 season.

items.title: Grading the Hellebuyck trade: Devils (finally) get their goalie as Jets head for uncertain future
items.summary: As Winnipeg laments the loss of a franchise legend, Jersey GM Mehta looks like a genius.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images The Connor Hellebuyck era is over in Winnipeg . The signature player of the Jets’ second iteration, Hellebuyck won everything but the Stanley Cup in Manitoba, collecting three Vezina Trophies and a Hart Trophy. Hellebuyck had grown vocally discontent with Winnipeg’s lackluster follow-up to a Presidents’ Trophy win in 2024-25, though, having apparently lost confidence that the Jets in front of him could compete as he waded into his late prime. Suspended without pay for skipping camp, ‘Bucky’ crossed the Rubicon and forced an exit from the only organization he’s ever known. An acrimonious end to a brilliant tenure in the prairies opened the door for the New Jersey Devils and GM Sunny Mehta, who had kept his interest in a player his predecessor, Tom Fitzgerald, had long courted close to the vest. The Devils have been searching for a goalie since Corey Schneider’s prime, which, as you may know, was a while ago. They have one now in Hellebuyck, who would walk into the Hall of Fame on his first try if he retired today. Will he do what Jacob Markstrom could not and complete Jersey’s Cup-contention puzzle? The Jets, meanwhile, have needed an out from their reliance on Hellebuyck and a thirtysomething core for some time. That one seed back in 2025 felt like this roster’s last real chance at the Cup during its collective prime, and a scorched-earth rebuild was never on the cards given how closely Winnipeg’s survival as a franchise is tied to its season-ticket sales. That means getting value via trades in lean years, especially for players of Hellebuyck’s quality. Can Dawson Mercer, young Alexander Command, and Co. help the Jets delay their decline? items.body: On a day dominated by Connor Hellebuyck, the Winnipeg Jets have been making other moves behind the scenes. Vlad Namestnikov has been placed on injured reserve retroactively following an injury picked up on October 15. The forward started the season with just one assist through six games for a lacklustre Jets team that sits 4-3-3. Other roster moves had to be made to make space for players coming in from the Hellebuyck trade, with Brayden Yager loaned to the Manitoba Moose and Jack St. Ivany placed on waivers, also for a loan to the Moose. Both players have featured on four occasions for the Jets this year, with neither registering a point. Winnipeg continues their season at home against the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday (7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT on Sportsnet and Sportsnet+), looking to snap a four-game losing streak.

items.body: The Edmonton Oilers will be without one of their top defenceman on Saturday. Mattias Ekholm will be sidelined against the Toronto Maple Leafs (7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT on Sportsnet and Sportsnet+) with a concussion, head coach Mike Babcock told reporters on Friday. Ekholm suffered the concussion in a collision with Carolina's William Carrier in the third period of the Oilers' win over the Hurricanes on Thursday. He appeared to hit his head on the ice as he attempted to play the puck in his own zone before the hit from Carrier. He stayed on his knees as he was attended to by the trainers. Ekholm eventually got to his feet and made his way off the ice, but appeared unsteady and needed assistance from teammates.

The Capitals have had several days now to digest Tuesday’s disappointing 5-2 loss to the Los Angeles Kings , which saw Washington squander a two-goal lead and surrender five unanswered goals to the NHL’s last remaining winless team. After a day off Thursday, Capitals returned to the ice Friday at MedStar Capitals Iceplex for their second and final full practice before facing Buffalo. items.body: Connor McDavid ’s thermonuclear start to the season has been the top story in Edmonton, and for good reason. At this rate, the Oilers captain will secure his 10th career 100-point season two and a half weeks before Christmas and break Wayne Gretzky’s single-season record by a mere 45 points. But the Oilers’ stylistic transformation under new coach Mike Babcock has also played a part in the team’s 8-1-1 start. Specifically, Edmonton has ditched the run-and-gun approach and started dumping in pucks at a much higher clip, which in turn has improved its defensive play. “We want to limit turnovers, obviously,” McDavid told reporters earlier this week. “We’re talking about playing better defence, and part of that is being responsible with the puck and managing the puck. I think you’re seeing that throughout the lineup, understanding when’s the time to attack and when’s the time to get on the forecheck. We want to be a heavy team. We want to forecheck pucks back. (We’ve) done that at times. We’ve gotten away from it at times, and we don’t have success. items.body: The dynamic duo had a combined 10 points in the Oilers’ 6-5 shootout win over the Carolina Hurricanes Thursday night, a game that saw the two former Hart Trophy winners go toe-to-toe with the defending Stanley Cup champions. No matter which way you dice it: with Connor McDavid, the start to the season he’s had, is having absolutely jaw-dropping. This does not happen very often: he has broken a Wayne Gretzky record. That just doesn’t happen. McDavid broke the Oilers’ franchise record for most points in the first 10 games of a season with his 31st point Thursday night. He went into a game against the best team in the Eastern Conference, and I was sitting there going, “Hey, this is going to be a quieter night, Carolina is known for playing that tight defensive system … it was fun for McDavid to average 2.8 points per game while it lasted.” Then what does he do? He puts up five points, and the duo of him and Leon Draisaitl combine for 10 points. On Friday, Leafs defenseman Nick Blankenburg was placed on injured reserve. Toronto has also placed defenseman Marshall Rifai on injured reserve. In corresponding moves, the Leafs have called up defensemen Dakota Mermis and Cole McWard from their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Toronto Marlies. Blankenburg, 28, suffered an upper-body injury during Thursday’s 5-4 win over the New York Rangers . The injury occured when he was checked hard into the boards by Rangers forward Will Cuylle in the third period, forcing him to miss the remainder of the game. The Washington, Michigan native has a goal and an assist for two points in six games this season, averaging just over 13 minutes of ice time. He attended Toronto’s training camp this year on a professional tryout agreement and ultimately secured a one-year, $1.4 million contract . Blankenburg split last season between the Nashville Predators and Colorado Avalanche , notching eight goals and 16 assists for 24 points over a total of 61 games. He is now in his sixth NHL season after signing with the Columbus Blue Jackets as an undrafted free agent in 2022. Rifai, 28, will be out week-to-week with a lower-body injury. He has a goal and no assists in two games played for the Leafs this season, while averaging just over 14 minutes of ice time. items.body: One thing we can be sure of when evaluating the evolution of NHL hockey is: nobody’s getting less talented. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-USA TODAY Sports Edmonton Oilers’ defenseman Mattias Ekholm will be out at least one week after he suffered an upper-body injury during Thursday’s game against the Carolina Hurricanes , head coach Mike Babcock told reporters after the game. Ekholm, 36, was injured just seconds into the third period after Hurricanes’ forward William Carrier delivered a hit in the Oilers’ end. The Edmonton blueliner appeared to hit his head on the ice and was slow to get up, and his teammates helped him off the ice. He finished the game with 14:16 of ice time, and the Oilers would defeat the Hurricanes 6-5 in a shootout. Both Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl recorded five points and factored in on all five of Edmonton’s goals. McDavid now has 31 points and has become the fourth player in NHL history to register 30 points through the first 10 games of a season . Ekholm, a native of Borlange, Sweden, has one goal and two assists for three points , and has averaged 21:45 of ice time through 10 appearances. Now in his 15th NHL season, the 6-foot-4 defender has 93 goals and 311 assists for 404 points in 976 career regular-season games with the Oilers and Nashville Predators . He also has 13 goals and 47 assists for 60 points in 125 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. He was part of both of Edmonton’s Stanley Cup Final runs in 2024 and 2025, and was also part of the Predators’ 2017 appearance. Ekholm is in the first season of a three-year contract extension signed in October 2025. items.body: CALGARY – Amidst his latest post-game sideshow, Devin Cooley stopped dead in his tracks. “I already know the DMs I'm going to be getting from Team Tank: Just stop winning, idiot!” he chuckled, as if scrawling the words with his hands. “But we're going to keep doing our best, and keep trying to win.” His Calgary Flames had just won consecutive games for the first time since February, following up a win over the defending champs with a 2-1 squeaker over the Minnesota Wild Thursday. The common thread was Cooley, whose latest masterpiece was a 36-save clinic he punctuated with meanderings with the media sure to find their way all over the internet once again. A sampling from the NHL’s Most Interesting Man, who two days earlier went viral trying to explain the difference between playing with a conscious and an unconscious brain: “Yeah, just a lot of thoughts popping in the head, and say like, ‘you know, you can move on - you don't have to stick around here, go away,” he explained, wide-eyed and abnormally loud, to the assembled press. “And then sometimes the thoughts stick around and they're in your head for a while, and you're like, ‘OK, you can stick around, you can hang out here. I'm not gonna think about you, and you can hang out.’” What we think he was trying to say was that he maintained a level of chill that somehow allowed him to withstand a third-period onslaught that saw the Wild climb within one, only to be denied with a stop on the final shot while Cooley lay prone on his back. It gave the Flames their third win in four games, which is a bounce-back few saw coming after the team was outscored by more than a couple touchdowns their first five games. items.title: ‘It’s just not real’: McDavid makes even more history in Oilers’ shootout win
items.summary: It’s just obscene what Connor McDavid is doing in his 29-year old season, ripping through the competition even more surgically than in years past. On Thursday, he hit yet another milestone.
items.body: EDMONTON — It’s the curse that rides shotgun next to the absolute blessing of watching the sport’s finest talent on a nightly basis. Or playing with that player. After another five-point night by Connor McDavid , in a thrilling 6-5 win over Carolina on Thursday, this scribe was lucky enough/dutybound to perform the task of trying to find a new angle for the “How great a player is Connor McDavid?” storyline. I could publish of book my columns on this topic (it wouldn’t sell), and McDavid isn’t even 30 years old yet. And, of course, his teammates get to relive the weekly task of standing in front of a group of reporters, each of us trying to find a new route into the most travelled destination in Edmonton hockey history. AG — after Gretzky — of course. “Connor broke a Gretzky record: 31 points now in this first 10 games,” a media member said, inside a question for Leon Draisaitl. “Those are video-game numbers!” Draisaitl had five points Thursday as well. But there he stood, being asked the “How awesome is Connor?” question for about the 2,000th time in his career. “What do you want me to say? It's just not real,” Draisaitl said. “He's maybe the greatest player to ever play, in my books. It’s a pleasure to share the ice with him, a pleasure to learn from him every day. He deserves everything.” With a five-point night, McDavid set an Oilers record for the most points through 10 games in a season with 31, surpassing Wayne Gretzky in 1984-85. And McDavid is one of just four players — alongside Gretzky, Mario Lemieux (three times) and Mike Bossy — to start a season with 30 points in the first 10 games. items.title: Red Wings’ John Gibson leaves game with upper-body injury
items.summary: Gibson left the Red Wings’ game against the Canucks with an upper-body injury and did not return.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images The Detroit Red Wings announced on social media that goaltender John Gibson left Thursday night’s game against the Vancouver Canucks with an upper-body injury. He would not return. Gibson did not take the ice for the third period. However, he did not face any shots in the second frame, as the Red Wings outshot the Canucks 13-0. Gibson had stopped four of five shots in the opening period. Michal Postava, whom the team called up from their AHL affiliate in Grand Rapids one day earlier, stopped seven of eight shots faced in his NHL debut, and the Red Wings defeated the Canucks 5-2. Gibson, 33, is 2-3-1 with an .871 save percentage (SV%) and 3.35 goals against average (GAA) in seven appearances in 2025-26. Through 13 NHL seasons, the Pittsburgh native has a 235-242-68 record with an .909 SV% and 2.88 GAA in 570 career regular-season games with Detroit and Anaheim Ducks . He’s also appeared in 26 career Stanley Cup Playoff games, where he’s posted an 11-13 record with a .912 SV% and 2.80 GAA. Gibson was selected by the Ducks in the second round of the 2011 NHL Entry Draft. Across four AHL seasons, all with the Norfolk Admirals, he went 34-23-8 with a .921 SV% and 2.38 GAA in 70 appearances. He also spent two seasons playing junior hockey in the Ontario Hockey League with the Kitchener Rangers, where he went 38-19-1 with a .928 SV% and 2.60 GAA in 59 career games. The Red Wings are now 4-3-3 with 11 points through their first 10 games of the season.

items.title: ‘Dragged us into the fight’: Fourth line leads Maple Leafs to win
items.summary: The fourth line of Zack MacEwen, Teddy Blueger and Brandon Duhaime stepped up in a big way as the Maple Leafs beat the Rangers.
items.body: TORONTO — There was a moment, five minutes into the night, when it looked like this game might turn. The Toronto Maple Leafs had struck out to an early lead against the visiting New York Rangers, off another moment of brilliance from young Easton Cowan. But the Blueshirts had started pushing back, piling up chances. A Vladislav Gavrikov point shot had glanced off Mika Zibanejad’s stick and beaten Sergei Bobrovsky, quieting the Scotiabank Arena crowd. Then the blue-and-white’s blue-collar trio hopped over the boards and went to work. First it was Zack MacEwen , flying into the offensive zone and barreling into defender Marcus Pettersson behind the Rangers' net. Then it was Teddy Blueger cutting off Will Cuylle along the wall, forcing the puck back towards the cage once more. The Rangers tried to reorganize, to steady themselves — only to see Brandon Duhaime crash into Sean Durzi and push play back into the depths of New York’s zone yet again. Two more times, the Rangers tried to get the puck to safety, and two more times the Maple Leafs’ fourth-liners stuffed it back into their zone. A tone-setting sequence from the depth trio. But it was only the start of a banner night for the three veterans. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Seattle’s Chandler Stephenson preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to the goal . According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 11:21 (8:39 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.title: Nugent-Hopkins scores shootout winner to give Oilers victory over Hurricanes
items.summary: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins scored the shootout winner to give the Edmonton Oilers a 6-5 victory over the Carolina Hurricanes on Thursday night.
items.body: EDMONTON — Ryan Nugent-Hopkins scored the shootout winner to give the Edmonton Oilers a 6-5 victory over the Carolina Hurricanes on Thursday night. Leon Draisaitl and Connor McDavid both shone with two goals and three assists apiece for the Oilers (8-1-1) who have won three straight and seven of their last eight. Nugent-Hopkins, who also had an assist, scored the other goal in regulation. Jackson Blake, Sebastian Aho, Seth Jarvis, Logan Stankhoven and Juuso Valimaki replied for the Hurricanes (8-2-2). The reigning Stanley Cup champions have lost two of their last three games. Hurricanes: Jarvis scored in his first game of the season, making his debut following off-season shoulder surgery. The 24-year-old has had more than 30 goals in each of the last three seasons. Oilers: Nugent-Hopkins also scored in his season debut, returning after sustaining a lower-body injury during training camp. The 33-year-old became the franchise leader for most seasons played with the Oilers at 16. Edmonton tied the game with their goalie pulled with 1:28 to play. McDavid sent a shot on net that deflected off Jesperi Kotkaniemi’s skate for his eighth goal of the season. McDavid, who has points in every game this season, extended his league-leading point totals to 31 in just 10 games. He joined Mario Lemieux, Mike Bossy and Wayne Gretzky as the only NHL players to reach the 30-point mark in 10 games or fewer. Hurricanes: Conclude a five-game road trip in St. Louis on Saturday. Oilers: Continue their homestand against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday.

items.title: ‘Easy to feel special’: Troy Stecher plays hero as Maple Leafs win thriller
items.summary: If some of his previous six NHL teams took Troy Stecher for granted, the Maple Leafs have not. The undersized waiver pick-up delivered the last-minute winner in a huge win over the Rangers on Thursday.
items.body: TORONTO — As the final minute of a tied-up barnburner sizzles away, Nick Paul gets hauled down illegally by Tye Kartye in the New York Rangers’ zone but keeps the puck alive and the penalty delayed with a second effort. Brandon Duhaime gathers Paul’s loose change and feeds it back to Morgan Rielly. Thinking pass all the way, the defenceman holds the puck on his blade, drawing in weak-side winger Will Cuylle as long as possible before zipping the thing across to partner Troy Stecher . Stecher, No. 28, cuts in, snaps his first shot of the game and bulges the back of Dylan Garand’s net with just 28 seconds to go. Then the undersized waiver gem — Brad Treliving’s parting gift to a roster his predecessor overhauled something fierce — throws a fist pump high as his shot, hugs his teammates, motions for Scotiabank Arena to raise to its feet, high-fives the line, then waves to the crowd again. This time with both arms. “Dating back to last year, I’ve really embraced being a Maple Leaf. So much passion around the city and so much love for the Leafs that, as a player, it’s really hard not to feel. Like, it’s pretty easy to feel special,” says Stecher, explaining his celebration after a 5-4 thriller on Thursday. “So, just trying to bring the arena together. You know, it’s more than just us 20 in here. It’s a big-time fan base, and I feel fortunate to be a part of it.” Thing is, Stecher has felt part of something similar, way back when he was playing 20-plus minutes a night in college and earning NHL attention the undrafted way. “A way different magnitude, but I did play at North Dakota. The Wild, who took three minor penalties in the first 14 minutes of the game, halved the deficit at 4:39 of the third period. The Flames were without captain Mikael Backlund, who's listed as day-to-day with an upper-body injury. Former Wild centre Ben Jones made his season debut for Calgary. Wild: Blake Coleman made his return to Calgary after spending five seasons as a Flame. Coleman and Olli Maatta were traded to the Wild last summer for Jacob Middleton and three draft picks. items.title: Oilers’ McDavid becomes fourth NHLer ever to register 30 points in first 10 games
items.summary: McDavid joins Mike Bossy, Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux as the only players to achieve the feat after a five-point night.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Just when you think you’ve seen it all from Connor McDavid, he continues to one-up himself. During Thursday night’s game against the Carolina Hurricanes , the Edmonton Oilers ‘ captain became the fourth player in NHL history to get 30 points in his first 10 games of a season with a five-point night. McDavid joins some elite company in achieving this feat, as only Mike Bossy, Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux have managed to get 30 points in the first 10 games of a season. Bossy and Gretzky have only achieved the feat once, both doing so in the 1984-85 season, while Lemieux did it three times in 1988-89, 1992-93 and 1995-96, the quickest coming in 1988-89 when he hit 30 points in only eight games. Bossy and Gretzky went on to put up a respective 117 and 208 points in 1984-85, while Lemieux had 199, 160 and 161 in his three respective seasons. This also makes McDavid the first player to achieve this feat in 31 years, and the first to do so in the 21st century. McDavid achieved the feat early in the third period of the game with the secondary assist on the 4-4 goal from Leon Draisaitl. At the start of a power play, McDavid had won the faceoff to Evan Bouchard, and after the Oilers center received a return pass, he then sent the puck across the ice to Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, who set up Draisaitl in front of the net for a one-timer goal. The assist was McDavid’s fourth point in the game, as he had gotten points on all four goals at the time. Brandon Duhaime, with a goal and two assists, Teddy Blueger, Kirill Marchenko and Easton Cowan provided the rest of the offence for Toronto (6-4-2). Sergei Bobrovsky made 21 saves. Mika Zibanejad, with a goal and an assist, Oliver Bjorkstrand, Tye Kartye and Alexis Lafrenière replied for New York (7-4-1), which got 31 stops from Dylan Garand. Adam Fox chipped in four assists. Stecher's winner came on a delayed penalty after he took a pass from Morgan Rielly and ripped a shot upstairs. After the teams traded goals inside the game's first six minutes, Blueger put Toronto ahead with his first for the club at 10:01 on a shot that just dribbled over the line. New York evened things 2-2 at 2:37 of the second when Bjorkstrand beat Bobrovsky from in tight. The visitors nudged in front at 6:30 when Kartye tipped home a point shot, but Duhaime buried his own rebound 90 seconds later — also his first goal in blue and white — to get Toronto level again. Marchenko gave the home side the lead with 50 seconds left in the period on a power play, but Lafrenière knotted the score again at 14:25 of the third. Bobrovsky tied Rangers legend Henrik Lundqvist for the most wins by a non-North American goaltender with 459. The pair now share sixth on the all-time list. items.body: San Jose Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov made an incredible diving glove save to stop a sure goal off a rocket from Ottawa Senators forward Drake Batherson at Canadian Tire Centre on Thursday. The Senators had a man advantage with defenseman Jake Sanderson controlling the puck at the point. Sanderson went cross-ice to forward Tim Stutzle at the right circle. Askarov moved to his left to play a shot from Stutzle, but he opted to go back across the ice to Batherson, who had a pretty open net. Askarov, a right-hand catcher, made a huge dive to his right and snagged Batherson's shot out of midair. Even with some traffic in front of the net, Askarov was still able to get there with the dive, looking more like a Gold Glove shortstop than a hockey goalie. Earlier in the game, Askarov made a pretty nice pad save on a Shane Pinto breakaway chance. After the diving save, he laid on the ice for a second and waited for the whistle. Take the rest, Yaroslav. You earned it.

Here is the latest lineup/injury news around the NHL. Seth Jarvis made his season debut for the Hurricanes at the Edmonton Oilers on Thursday. The forward had surgery in June to repair a torn labrum and rotator cuff in his right shoulder. He was a full participant at Hurricanes practice Wednesday, skating on a line with Jordan Martinook and Jesperi Kotkaniemi , and took part in an optional skate Thursday. "I'm ready to play and now it's up to the coaching staff whether they want me in or not," Jarvis said. items.body: Register Login East Notes: Chatfield, Cousins, Tkachuk By Ethan Hetu | at October 22, 2026 6:35 pm The Carolina Hurricanes did a remarkable job retaining nearly the entirety of their Stanley Cup-winning roster from last season. But with another year set to go by, it seems almost certain that the club will lose at least some players from their championship roster. One player that could depart is pending UFA defenseman Jalen Chatfield . David Pagnotta of The Fourth Period reported yesterday that the Hurricanes and Chatfield’s agent, Darren Ferris of Quartexx, attempted to negotiate an extension, but those talks did not result in pen hitting paper. Pagnotta noted that there “have been no talks since” between Ferris and the Hurricanes, and added that the “inkling right now is that [Chatfield] is headed to free agency.” Chatfield, could be set to cash in on the open market after becoming a steady contributor to the Hurricanes’ defense over the last half-decade. A fleet-footed undrafted blueliner, Chatfield was plucked from the Canucks organization as a free agent and broke into the NHL after one season spent developing with Carolina’s AHL affiliate, the Chicago Wolves. After winning a Calder Cup in Chicago, Chatfield established himself at the NHL level. He was a seamless fit for the way head coach Rod Brind’Amour wants his defensemen to play, and his ability to leverage his above-average skating to close out on pucks quickly and play aggressively has made him a valuable secondary defensive piece for the club. Now 30 years old, Chatfield’s upcoming free agency represents his best chance at earning a life-changing contract. Based on Pagnotta’s reporting, it seems Chatfield might end up receiving that contract, just maybe not from the Hurricanes.

items.title: Panthers’ Cooper Black becomes tallest goalie to play NHL game
items.body: PITTSBURGH — Florida Panthers goalie Cooper Black skated onto the PPG Paints Arena ice alone during pregame warmups on Thursday night, a time-honoured hockey tradition given to rookies everywhere. It took Black fewer strides to make the memorable lap than most. Black made NHL history in his first career start when he became the tallest goaltender to ever appear in a regular-season game. Black is listed as two inches taller than Ben Bishop, Ivan Fedotov, Mads Sogaard and Mikko Koskinen, all 6-foot-7. The 25-year-old from Alpen, Michigan, who started playing when he was 8 and had a 5-inch growth spurt between his junior and senior years in high school when he shot up from 6 feet to 6 feet 5 inches and kept right on going, was excellent in his first period. Black, called up from Florida's AHL affiliate in Charlotte recently after Jacob Markstrom went down with a shoulder injury, stopped Pittsburgh Penguins defenseman Kris Letang with his blocker pad on a wrist shot about two minutes in. He also turned aside a breakaway opportunity by Penguins forward Rickard Rakell before giving up a goal to Nick Robertson, who beat Black to the glove side. Panthers head coach Paul Maurice praised Black's development in recent years. Florida signed Black as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2024. Black blossomed last season in Charlotte, posting a 25-13-4 record with a 2.47 goals against average and a .903 save percentage. “A man that size, it takes a long time to grow into that body,” Maurice said before adding with a laugh, “I think he’s done.”

items.title: Remembering The Life And Legacy Of Rangers Star Ron Duguay
items.summary: The 12-year NHL star has passed away after a long battle with cancer.
items.body: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports Remembering The Life And Legacy Of Rangers Star Ron Duguay Ken Campbell Partner Oct 22, 2026 8:15 PM Published Oct 22, 2026 8:15 PM Updated Oct 22, 2026 8:55 PM The 12-year NHL star has passed away after a long battle with cancer. Most hockey fans remember Ron Duguay as a the perfectly coiffed cult star of the New York Rangers . And he deserves all of the recognition he gets as one of the most popular players in franchise history. But Duguay, who died of cancer at the age of 69 on Wednesday, was even more popular and dynamic as a member of the Sudbury Wolves in the mid-1970s, when he led a team that did everything but win an Ontario League championship. That was where he first displayed his blazing speed, on-ice elegance and soft touch before being drafted by the Rangers in the first round of the 1977 draft. More Videos He was truly an iconic player, one who thrived on the scene in New York. And even though he's not in the Hockey Hall of Fame, those of us from Northern Ontario will always look fondly at his No. 10, which hangs in the rafters of the Sudbury Arena.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Positive news for the Minnesota Wild as they continue their road trip through Western Canada. The team activated captain Jared Spurgeon from injured reserve, making him available to be in the lineup on Thursday night, when the Wild visit the Calgary Flames . It will be the veteran defenseman’s first action in four games. He was placed on IR with an upper-body injury on Sunday, retroactive to Oct. 12, when he helped the Wild pick up a win over the Vegas Golden Knights. With Spurgeon out of the lineup, the Wild held firm, but weren’t amazing. They fell to the surprising Winnipeg Jets before beating the St. Louis Blues seven days ago. Then, after beating the Columbus Blue Jackets on Sunday, Minnesota managed to rally from a 3-1 deficit to salvage a point against the Edmonton Oilers , only to lose in overtime. In Minnesota’s first six games of the 2026-27 campaign, the 36-year-old scored a goal and four assists for five points, tied for fifth on the team in helpers. Spurgeon has a plus/minus of +4, while averaging 22:21 of ice time. Staying in the lineup and out of the press box has been tough for Spurgeon throughout his NHL career. Only one of the Edmonton native’s 17 seasons saw him appear in every game, that coming during the 2018-19 campaign. He did play in 79 games last year, which came just two years after Spurgeon was limited to a mere 16 contests. In 1.018 regular-season games in the NHL, Spurgeon has posted 124 goals and 319 assists for 443 points, with another 31 points in 84 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. items.body: TORONTO -- Dave Maloney was never surprised to see how Ron Duguay valiantly fought his battle with cancer. It was with a positive attitude and a zest for life that had come to define the way Duguay lived until he died Thursday at the age of 69. “It was commendable, it was commendable to his family,” Maloney told NHL.com on Thursday. “His daughters really, and his son, his family, were really the basis for his fight. We're culturally, as hockey guys, we're not going to give up, right? I just think that it was admirable but I wouldn't expect anything other than that from who I knew him to be when we were all young.” Maloney and Duguay were teammates with the New York Rangers for six seasons, from 1977-83, which began when Maloney was 21 and Duguay was 20. Maloney said Duguay, and Dave’s brother, Don, who joined the Rangers for the 1978-79 season, stood out to him for being on the forefront of physical fitness during an era where the expectations that players face today were not the same. “He and my brother were two guys that were ahead of the curve believe it or not, in taking care of themself,” Maloney said. “I know the dynamic story of Ron and there's a lot of reality to those dynamic stories, believe me, but he took care of himself. He really did. He was physically fit. His father was a fitness guy. items.body: 19-year-old forward lost consciousness, still 'clearly shaken,' GM says CRANBERRY, Pa. -- Ben Kindel could return to practice as soon as next week after losing consciousness aboard the Pittsburgh Penguins team plane Tuesday, general manager Kyle Dubas said Thursday. The 19-year-old forward was cleared to travel to Pittsburgh on Wednesday after experiencing a vasovagal syncope, a sudden drop in heart rate and blood pressure that reduces blood flow to the brain, about 10 minutes after the plane departed Salt Lake City International Airport. Kindel received oxygen before an emergency medical landing and was transported to the University of Utah medical center. Kindel, who played 18:53 in a 5-4 loss at the Utah Mammoth on Monday, was placed on injured reserve Thursday. He will have increased testing and could begin training in the next four days if there are no complications, Dubas said. "I mean, so tough to put a timeframe on it," Dubas said. "We play tonight. We play Saturday night. ... Our hope is to get everything done, tested, back into training here in the next four days or so and see if he can return to practice on Sunday or Monday. "That's why I would put an asterisk on that by saying 'we'll see how everything goes before then.'" Kindel has four points (two goals, two assists) in nine games this season, his second since being selected by Pittsburgh in the first round (No. 11) of the 2025 NHL Draft. He had 35 points (17 goals, 18 assists) in 77 games as a rookie. "Happy everything is alright," defenseman Erik Karlsson said. "We're moving on from that. He began working with the Rangers in the 1954-55 season as an assistant publicist. In 1955, he began covering the Rangers as the beat writer for Hearst's New York Journal-American and has been writing about the team ever since, including his weekly column on NHL.com. Today, he writes about Ron Duguay , a Rangers legend from the 1970s and 80s, who died Thursday at the age of 69. He was like Mr. Manhattan -- suave, handsome with a winning smile, a big heart. items.body: Register Login Canadiens’ Nick Suzuki Out 2-4 Weeks, Owen Beck Recalled By Bradley Keith | at October 22, 2026 11:19 am One of the longest iron man streaks in league history has met an unfortunate end, as Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki will be out 2-4 weeks with an upper-body injury, the team announced . Owen Beck has been recalled from AHL Laval as a result. Montreal won’t have #14 in the lineup for the first time since Game 82 of the 2018-19 season, a win over Toronto where Andrew Shaw recorded two points, serving as an indication of just how long it has been. Having yet to miss a single appearance now in year eight, Suzuki’s 546-game streak will close out at 20th all time in NHL history and the second-longest out of active players behind Brent Burns ’ 1,017. In their last contest, an overtime defeat at the hands of the Sharks, the center led all forwards with 21:03 of ice time. It’s not entirely clear when the injury occurred, although before the news even dropped Eric Engels of Sportsnet pointed out that the 2026 Selke winner took a shot to the hand in the San Jose game and had to receive treatment post-game. A star who obviously requires a lot to be out of the lineup, one can assume from that report that a relatively serious hand injury occurred. Breaking out last season with 101 points as a bonafide superstar, the 27-year-old has continued that pace into this season with 12 points in nine games. Few can impact the game in as many areas as he can, leading both the power play and penalty kill, logging heavy minutes at 21:47, fifth most in the NHL out of forwards. With high expectations, his Habs have come out of the gate a bit slower than hoped with a 4-3-2 record.
